scenario_name: Admin account bulk user-object modification burst
notes: Injected: 320 user-object modifications in one day against a 30-day baseline of 3-6. Primary change-velocity positive; should score near 1.0.
Injected: HR sync identity writes to 47 groups in one day; baseline is attribute-only updates. Tests that a service account with a stable baseline is still scored.

scenario_name: Off-hours mass OU and GPO restructure
notes: Injected: 88 OU/GPO edits between 02:00 and 04:00 Saturday. Exercises the off_hours_ratio feature as well as raw volume.

scenario_name: Compromised helpdesk account mass password reset
notes: Injected: 210 EventCode 4724 resets in 40 minutes. Volume and dc_targets both far outside baseline.
Injected: 135 computer objects deleted in one window; act_deleted dominates the action mix.

scenario_name: Delegated OU admin mass group additions
notes: Injected: delegated admin adds 60 service accounts to groups outside its delegated OU. Lower absolute volume; tests sensitivity at the low end.
Benign high volume by design: ~900 objects created every quarter-end. Recurs inside the 30-day training window so the fitted distribution should absorb it. A detection here is a false positive.
Benign: 40-70 resets every working day, near-zero off-hours. Classic high-but-stable volume account.

scenario_name: Nightly HR to AD attribute sync
notes: Benign: runs 23:50 nightly so off_hours_ratio is permanently 1.0. Tests that off-hours alone does not drive a detection.
Cold start: account has only 5 days of feature rows. The fit search drops accounts with fewer than 7 observed days, so this must produce no score at all.
Benign: change-approved DC promotion generates a one-day burst that is present in the labeled corpus as an approved change. Expected false positive source; documented, not suppressed.
Injected: account whose peer cluster is 100% Service/Batch logons produces 6 Interactive (type 2) logons. Highest-signal peer deviation case.
Injected: standard desktop user opens Remote Interactive sessions to 14 servers in one day; r_remote_interactive and log_dest_hosts both spike.
Injected: burst of 4768/4771 events with an elevated failure ratio against an otherwise silent service principal.

scenario_name: Batch logon type appears for a human administrator
notes: Injected: scheduled-task (type 4) logons under an interactive admin identity - persistence-shaped, low volume, deliberately near the detection floor.
Injected: Network Cleartext (type 8) logons at 03:00; r_network_cleartext is zero for the whole peer cluster.
Benign: source hosts and IPs change but the logon-type mix is unchanged. The model is deliberately behavioural, not geographic, so this must not score.
Cold start: fewer than 7 observed days, so the fit excludes the account. Detection here indicates the days_observed guard has regressed.
Benign: dormant for 20 days then 10 days of Batch logons. Volume changes, logon-type ratios do not.
Benign: routine Remote Interactive sessions to many desktops - the whole helpdesk peer cluster looks like this, so peer_z should stay low.
Benign: 100% Service logons, 100% off-hours, high host fan-out - extreme in absolute terms but typical for its cluster. Tests peer-relative rather than absolute scoring.

scenario_name: User added directly to Domain Admins
notes: Injected: new_reach at min_depth 1. Highest weighted privilege-path case (depth weight 1.0 x change weight 1.0).

scenario_name: Application owner group nested under Enterprise Admins
notes: Injected: a populated group is nested one level below a Tier-0 group, granting 23 members effective Tier-0 in a single change.

scenario_name: Distribution list nested into Account Operators
notes: Injected: distribution list used as a security path - the nesting case the deterministic critical-group searches miss.

scenario_name: Privilege path depth decreased three to one
notes: Injected: deployment account moved from a 3-hop nested path to direct membership. Tests the depth_decreased classification, not new_reach.
Injected: account already reachable to one Tier-0 group gains two more. Tests the reach_increased classification (change weight 0.6).
Injected: nested group re-parented under Backup Operators at depth 2. Tests depth-2 scoring (depth weight 0.75).
Benign: permanent Domain Admins member across the whole corpus window. Classified unchanged, so no risk row should ever be written.
Benign: CN changes but the DN-keyed path and depth do not. The baseline diff is keyed on entity_dn, so a rename must not read as a new path.

scenario_name: Member removed from a critical group
notes: Benign for this model: privilege reduction. Depth increases or reach drops, which is not one of the three alerting classifications.
Benign: heavy nesting churn with no path to any critical or adminCount=1 group, so the seed set never reaches it.

Cold start: the very first PrivPath run against an empty baseline must write zero risk rows. Entity exists in the corpus with a depth-2 path to a critical group from day one; the promotion-only first run must not classify it as new_reach.
